Scott K. Field

Republican candidate for 15th Court of Appeals, Place 2, Texas

Justice, Texas Fifteenth Court of Appeals (Place 2)

Scott K. Field is the sitting justice in Place 2 of the Texas Fifteenth Court of Appeals. Gov. Greg Abbott appointed him on June 11, 2024, and he took office on September 1, 2024, when the court was created. He won the Republican primary on March 3, 2026, and faces Democrat Tom Baker in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Field stands

Judicial philosophy
Says judges should apply the law as written and not rewrite it to fit personal views or political outcomes. Says the Constitution, statutes and precedents should be interpreted and applied fairly and consistently.
Judicial independence and impartiality
Says every case deserves impartial review based on the law, not politics, and that Texans deserve a judiciary that is independent, even-handed and faithful to the Constitution.

Background

  • Justice, Texas Fifteenth Court of Appeals, Place 2 (2024–present; appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott)
  • Judge, 480th District Court, Williamson County (2023–2024; first judge of the court)
  • Justice, Texas Third Court of Appeals, Place 3 (2012–2018; lost re-election in 2018 to Chari Kelly)
  • Private practice: The Field Law Firm; partner at York, Keller & Field, L.L.P.; Baker Botts, L.L.P.
  • Law clerk to Justice Raul Gonzalez, Supreme Court of Texas
  • J.D., University of Texas School of Law (1995)
  • B.A., political science, Texas A&M University (1992)
  • Lives in Liberty Hill, Texas
